## Personality

Josie Pye is known for her disagreeable nature, sharp tongue, and lack of imagination, often perceived by her peers as a cheat. Unbothered by the need to earn a living, her primary motivation for pursuing a college education is simply for education's sake. Among her noted talents are an innate ability for walking board fences and a proven skill in crafting knitted lace, for which she has won a first prize.

## History

Josie Pye is the last of the [Pye](../codex/factions.md#pyes) family to attend [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) school, and she famously took first prize for knitted lace at the exhibition. During a party at [Diana](../character/diana.md) Barry's house, Josie dared [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, which resulted in [Anne](../character/anne.md) falling and breaking her ankle. She later attended school under Miss [Stacy](../character/stacy.md) and was among the group of local students who studied alongside [Anne](../character/anne.md) and [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md). Josie eventually left home to attend Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) in town with her [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) classmates to earn her teaching license. Upon completing her studies, she graduated from Queen's alongside her peers, who celebrated various academic achievements, including scholarships and medals.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P1](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER XV. ## Relationships

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--josie-pye.md)

Josie Pye and [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) maintain an adversarial relationship marked by mutual dislike, unkind comments, and bitter rivalry. During a gathering at Diana's house, Josie pushes their competitive dynamic to a dangerous limit by daring [Anne](../character/anne.md) to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, which causes [Anne](../character/anne.md) to fall and break her ankle. Their antagonism persists at school, where they compete directly as classmates both in social dares and later as peers in Miss Stacy's advanced class preparing for the Queen's [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) examination.

- Enemy of — mutual dislike and unkind comments  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXVII. Vanity and Vexation of Spirit P40](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0040)</sub>
- Rival of — exchanging dares and competing in acts of daring  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006)</sub>
